title: Atomic billing semantics for speculative prefetch + rerank chains on non-chat endpoints
creator: Evelyn Huang
description: Problem: Non-chat endpoints (embeddings + rerank + structured tool invocations) are increasingly using speculative prefetches and hedged rerank calls to reduce latency. Prefetches and speculative tool bootstraps cause multi-stage executions where only a subset of stages are used to produce final output. Current metering charges are inconsistent: customers sometimes get charged for speculative prefetches without clear refund semantics, and partial failures lead to ambiguous audit trails. This ticket defines atomic billing semantics and an implementation plan for per-stage microcrediting, deterministic refunds, and an auditable ledger for multi-stage non-chat flows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each non-chat multi-stage flow (prefetch -> rerank -> tool invocation) emits a single canonical usage record per API request with per-stage breakdown.
decision_log:
- Decided to implement a two-phase meter commit: a provisional pre-authorization (microcredit hold) at request admission, and a final commit/adjust action after the request resolves.
- Use a deterministic idempotent checkpoint ID (ledger_id) per top-level api call to correlate speculative sub-requests.
- Refund semantics: partial/unused prefetch tokens are reclaimed and attributed to a 'heuristic-refund' bucket; refunds visible in billing export within 15 minutes.
- Trade-offs: this introduces a small amount of additional DB writes and a short-lived provisional state. We prioritized correctness and auditability over absolute minimal write amplification.
implementation_plan:
1) Server-side API layer: add ledger_id injection at the admission layer for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, structured-tool).
2) Metering service: extend MeterRecords table with columns: ledger_id (string), stage (prefetch|rerank|tool), provisional_hold (boolean), finalized (boolean), effective_tokens (integer). Since data model changes must be backward compatible, keep existing overall invoice item aggregation unchanged until rollout.
3) Admission path will create a provisional_hold record for speculative prefetch calls with a small initial token estimate.
4) On finalization, the runtime computes effective_tokens per stage, issues commit that sets finalized=true and delta_tokens is applied to invoice. If delta is negative (refund), create a refund record linked to ledger_id.
5) Add a reconciliation job that scans provisional holds older than 1 hour and forces a safety finalization and flags anomalies for ops.
6) Provide SDK/headers to allow customers to opt into 'immediate-charge' mode (legacy behavior) for compatibility.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of non-chat traffic within a single region to new metering model, enable verbose logging and ledger debug export to internal dashboard.
Phase 2: Open beta for high-usage customers with opt-in header.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring and reconcile windows of increasing size.
Backout: revert admission-side ledger_id injection and run reconcile to close provisional holds.
Communication: post migration notes and sample billing exports in Console -> Billing Insights.
monitoring_kpis:
- Ratio of provisional_hold -> finalized within 60s (>99.5% target).
- Refunds issued per 10k requests (should be stable and explainable).
- Incorrect double-charges (alert if > 0.01% of requests).
- Reconciliation job anomalies count.
- Billing export latency (target < 15m for refunds visibility).
migration_steps:
1) Run DB migration to add ledger_id and flags (backfill with NULL for historical).
2) Deploy metering service change in staging, run synthetic flows with speculative prefetches and tool errors to validate ledger lifecycle.
3) Enable canary for 5% traffic and run reconcile checks.
4) Run a 48h smoke comparing old vs new invoice aggregates to ensure parity within error bounds.
5) Gradually flip beta customers and monitor.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for ledger lifecycle (create provisional, commit with delta, refund path).
- Integration test: end-to-end synthetic flow with deliberate tool failure to assert refund is generated and final invoice line is consistent.
- Load test: ensure metering writes sustain peak throughput (target 10k RPS provisional holds without >5% latency regression).
- Chaos test: drop finalization events to ensure reconciliation job picks up and resolves stales.
- Acceptance: billing export ingest in data warehouse must show ledger_id correlation and reconcile to expected totals.
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial triage — assigned to Ravi. Scoped as P0 after billing incident with a major customer (postmortem ENG-2026-02-bill-incident-1).

2026-02-20: Prototype completed for ledger_id propagation and provisional_hold creation. Microbenchmark shows +3.2% tail p95 on admission under synthetic load. Decision: optimize by batching ledger writes in 50ms window.
2026-02-28: Design review with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Finance (Marcus Cole). Finance requested explicit refund visibility in Console and a CSV export. Added refund record shape to schema.
2026-03-03: Security review kickoff — no secrets involved; data model and logs reviewed for PII. Security requested retention limits for provisional records (30 days) — added to migration plan.
2026-03-08: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15 for us-west-2. Ops runbook drafted.

notes: Be careful to keep the new metering records idempotent to avoid double-commits from retries. Use tenant-scoped ledger_id derivation (sha256(request_id + tenant_id + timestamp_window)) to guarantee uniqueness while supporting replay. Coordinate with Console team to add a 'per-call ledger trace' view before GA.
